curated.instructions: omr/instructions/850-1/ (scans; the fork lift is pages 1-8, alternate models after)

functions.does: The handwheel on the mast's left side raises and lowers the forks: the axle across the top of the mast carries two small gears that run up and down the carriage's two long racks.
functions.source: book: forks steps 1-3, main steps 11-13 and the cover photo; the handwheel, the 24-tooth gear and both rack pinions share the top axle
functions.note: The book's step 13 adds a second axle 10 below the mast-top axle, with an 8-tooth gear meshing the 24-tooth gear; the model file leaves out that axle and gear, so its 24-tooth gear meshes with nothing. What the lower axle is for is unsure (inferred: perhaps a slower crank, or a brake).

functions.does: The steering wheel steers the back wheels: its upright axle turns a crown gear, which drives a 24-tooth gear on a lengthwise axle, whose 8-tooth gear at the back slides the steering rack between the two wheel turntables.
functions.source: book: steering steps 1-5, main steps 6-7, 9 and 12

functions.does: The four wheels roll freely; the front pair are on short axles of their own.
The two levers beside the seat tip fore and aft on their pins, as the driver's controls; they work nothing.
functions.source: inferred: book steps 10-11 put an axle 4 in a pin connector on a sideways pin at each side of the seat; no motion is drawn

questions.question: Book step 13 adds an axle under the mast-top axle with an 8 tooth gear on the 24 tooth gear. What is it for: a slower crank, or a brake? Are the levers by the seat just decoration?
